content.title: We're tracking all games, perfect brackets in the 2026 NCAA tournament
content.text: Sort By:Oldest FirstLatest2:32 pm, March 26, 2026 If you missed out on some of the Sweet 16 teams in your bracket, don't worry. Pretty much everyone did. Only 11 brackets out of the millions in the Men's Bracket Challenge Game correctly picked all Sweet 16 teams. That's fewer than last year, when 113 got all 16 right. Most brackets got between nine and 12 teams right, as 70.609 percent of MBCG brackets landed in that window. Though seven of the top eight teams are still left, No. 9 Iowa knocked out defending national champion and No. 1 Florida — and all four top seeds made the Sweet 16 in both 2024 and 2025. No. 11 Texas also went from the First Four to the Sweet 16. Those Hawkeyes and Longhorns are the biggest reasons why brackets missed some Sweet 16 teams. Only 5.64 percent had Iowa in the Sweet 16 and only 5.52 percent had Texas making the second weekend. On the opposite end, No. 1 Duke made it this far on 92.31 percent of brackets. Here's the rundown of the percent of brackets that got Sweet 16 teams correct: 0 out of 16: 0.482% 1 out of 16: 0.249% 2 out of 16: 0.443% 3 out of 16: 0.756% 4 out of 16: 1.373% 5 out of 16: 2.345% 6 out of 16: 3.679% 7 out of 16: 5.881% 8 out of 16: 9.945% 9 out of 16: 19.029% 10 out of 16: 19.123% 11 out of 16: 18.770% 12 out of 16: 13.687% 13 out of 16: 3.712% 14 out of 16: 0.506% 15 out of 16: 0.020% 16 out of 16: 0.0002% 4:03 am, March 23, 2026 The 3-pointers kept falling as No. 4 Alabama rolled No. 5 Texas Tech, 90-65, to reach the Sweet 16. The Crimson Tide hit 19 3-pointers on the night and never were challenged by the Red Raiders. Latrell Wrightsell sank six 3-pointers to score a game-high 24 points. He was one of seven Alabama players to make a 3-pointer, including Houston Mallette and his five 3-pointers. Alabama is in the Sweet 16 for the fourth consecutive year and will play top-seeded Michigan in Chicago. 3:26 am, March 23, 2026 Alex Karaban's career night lifted No. 2 UConn into the Sweet 16 and past UCLA, 73-57. Karaban scored a career-high 27 points on 9 for 16 shooting, making four 3-pointers. The Huskies trailed early but eventually separated themselves from UCLA. UConn held UCLA to only 39 percent shooting and won the rebounding battle 36-24. 78.36 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge Game entries had the Huskies in the Sweet 16, where they will take on No. 3 Michigan State. 2:30 am, March 23, 2026 Top-seeded Arizona withstood an offensive slump and second half Utah State push to become the third No. 1 seed to reach the Sweet 16, winning 78-66. It's the third year in a row the Wildcats are in the Sweet 16. The Wildcats, who led by as many as 18 points, saw their lead dwindle down to four before regrouping late to advance. Four players scored in double figures for the top seed, with Koa Peat (14 points, 10 rebounds) and Motiejus Krivas (11 points, 14 rebounds) both posting a double-double. Garry Clark scored 13 off the bench for the Aggies, who were attempting to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1970. 1:34 am, March 23, 2026 The defending champs are out. So is the first No. 1 seed in this year's tournament. No. 9 Iowa shocked top-seeded Florida 73-72 on Alvaro Folgueiras' late 3-pointer to add another dramatic finish to a wild Sunday in the second round. The Hawkeyes are now in the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1999 — just like St. John's accomplished earlier in the day. Florida was in the Sweet 16 on 89.65 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge Game entries, the third-highest mark. The Gators were the national champion on 6.62 percent of brackets. Iowa shot only 7 for 24 from distance yet Folgueiras' final shot took down the top seed. Florida got a combined 40 points from Alex Condon and Thomas Haugh, but a year after all four top seeds made the Final Four for only the second time ever, a top seed is out before the end of the first weekend. 12:11 am, March 23, 2026Here's a look at the nation's final perfect bracket: "christienter" in ESPN's game. Here's the complete rundown of this last perfect bracket's final picks for Sunday's games: "christienter" on ESPN — Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech 10:52 pm, March 22, 2026 A buzzer-beater means one bracket stands alone. St. John's Dylan Darling's driving layup — his only points of the game — beat the final horn and gave the Red Storm a thrilling 67-65 win against Kansas on Sunday in the second round after the Jayhawks tied the game in the final moments despite trailing by as many as 14 points. The Red Storm scored the final bucket to advance to the Sweet 16 and also eliminate two perfect brackets, leaving only one left. We've been tracking around 36 million brackets in the major online games (Men’s Bracket Challenge Game, ESPN, CBS, Yahoo!, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and Kalshi) since Thursday and now "christienter" in ESPN's game stands alone. Both Zuby Ejiofor and Bryce Hopkins scored 18 points for St. John's, which is in the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1999. Darryn Peterson scored 21 for Kansas, which shot 44 percent to the Red Storm's 36 but also committed 16 turnovers. The last perfect bracket is now 43-0 — officially surpassing last year’s final perfect bracket. We’ll see if "christienter" can keep it going into the Sweet 16. The longest perfect bracket we’ve seen was from Gregg Nigl in 2019, when he got the first 49 games correct. Here’s what the final perfect bracket has for the rest of Sunday as we close out the second round: "christienter" on ESPN — Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech 8:28 pm, March 22, 2026 After a slow start, Iowa State surged past Kentucky to advance to the Sweet 16 — and take out one of the last few perfect brackets. With the No. 2 Cyclones' 82-63 win against No. 7 Kentucky on Sunday, only three brackets are still perfect out of the around 36 million we've been tracking since Thursday afternoon. Tamin Lipsey had a big game for Iowa State, totaling 26 points, 10 assists and five steals as Kentucky committed 20 turnovers. We'll continue tracking the last three perfect brackets in the final six games of the day. Can one make it to the Sweet 16? That happened in 2019. Here's what the final three have for the rest of the day: "megs4525875" on MBCG — Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Alabama "christienter" on ESPN — St. John's, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech "Mini-mi-2448's Picks 24" on ESPN — Kansas, Tennessee, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech 5:47 pm, March 22, 2026 Thanks to No. 2 Purdue's big second half, the Boilermakers are off to the Sweet 16 and the last four brackets all make it to another game. No. 2 Purdue's 79-69 win against No. 7 Miami (Fla.) moved the four perfect brackets to 41-0 as Fletcher Loyer scored 24 points and Purdue outscored the Hurricanes by 12 in the second half. It's the third year in a row the Boilermakers are in the Sweet 16. They will play No. 11 Texas — the last remaining double-digit seed — on Thursday. There will be separation in the next game of No. 2 Iowa State vs. No. 7 Kentucky, as three of the brackets have the Cyclones and one has the Wildcats. Here are the upcoming picks for the rest of Sunday's games on the four brackets: "Cody DeRose" on MBCG — Kentucky, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech "megs4525875" on MBCG — Iowa State, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Alabama "christienter" on ESPN — Iowa State, St. John's, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech "Mini-mi-2448's Picks 24" on ESPN — Iowa State, Kansas, Tennessee, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech We'll continue to update you on the chase for perfection. 2:45 pm, March 22, 2026 Not only will the Sweet 16 field be set today, but we'll also see if any of the four remaining perfect brackets can make it through the eight-game slate. Going into Saturday, we had 207 perfect brackets nationally among the major online games (Men’s Bracket Challenge Game, ESPN, CBS, Yahoo!, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and Kalshi). Things stayed in the triple digits until No. 11 Texas upset No. 3 Gonzaga. No. 4 Nebraska then topped No. 5 Vanderbilt in a thriller to cut down the brackets from 26 to four. Now we wait to find out how long these four brackets can hang on. We believe the record for the longest start to a perfect bracket is 49 games, when Gregg Nigl didn't get a game wrong until the Sweet 16. Follow along with us as we track the picks of these four perfect brackets during Sunday's games: "Cody DeRose" on MBCG — Purdue, Kentucky, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech "megs4525875" on MBCG — Purdue, Iowa State, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Alabama "christienter" on ESPN — Purdue, Iowa State, St. John's, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech "Mini-mi-2448's Picks 24" on ESPN — Purdue, Iowa State, Kansas, Tennessee, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech Here's the full rundown of the Sunday schedule: No. 2 Purdue vs. No. 7 Miami (Fla.) | 12:10 p.m. ET on CBS No. 2 Iowa State vs. No. 7 Kentucky | 2:45 p.m. on CBS No. 4 Kansas vs. No. 5 St. John's | 5:15 p.m. on CBS No. 3 Virginia vs. No. 6 Tennessee | 6:10 p.m. on TNT No. 1 Florida vs. No. 9 Iowa | 7:10 p.m. on TBS No. 1 Arizona vs. No. 9 Utah State | 7:50 p.m. on truTV No. 2 UConn vs. No. 7 UCLA | 8:45 p.m. on TNT No. 4 Alabama vs. No. 5 Texas Tech | 9:45 p.m. on TBS 3:43 am, March 22, 2026 It's a perfect bracket version of the final four. With No. 4 Arkansas’ 94-88 win over No. 12 High Point, four perfect brackets will advance to the fourth day of the tournament. We began the day with 224 perfect brackets. No. 3 Michigan State’s win over No. 6 Louisville brought that number down to 133. Wins from No. 1 Duke and No. 2 Houston took out a few perfect brackets, bringing the total to 120. The big hitter of the day was when No. 11 Texas upset No. 3 Gonzaga, bringing the total number of perfect brackets down to 27. Just one of those had No. 11 VCU upsetting No. 3 Illinois, but the Illini won big. When No. 4 Nebraska took down No. 5 Vanderbilt in a thriller, it took out 22 perfect brackets with it, leaving just four heading into the final game of the night, all of which had Arkansas advancing to the Sweet 16. The four remaining brackets are split in the Men’s Bracket Challenge Game and ESPN. Here are the remaining brackets — two in the MBCG and two on ESPN — and their picks for Sunday's eight second round games: "Cody DeRose" on MBCG — Purdue, Kentucky, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech "megs4525875" on MBCG — Purdue, Iowa State, Kansas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Alabama "christienter" on ESPN — Purdue, Iowa State, St. John's, Virginia, Florida, Arizona, UConn, Texas Tech "Mini-mi-2448's Picks 24" on ESPN — Purdue, Iowa State, Kansas, Tennessee, Florida, Arizona, UCLA, Texas Tech We began this year’s tournament with more than 36 million brackets across major online games (Men’s Bracket Challenge Game, ESPN, CBS, Yahoo, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and Kalshi). Just over 14,000 made it past the first day unscathed. Only 224 were a perfect 32-for-32 in the first round. Here’s how we went from 224 to four on the third day of the men’s tournament: No. 1 Michigan 95, No. 9 Saint Louis 72 — 207 perfect No. 3 Michigan State 77, No. 6 Louisville 69 — 133 perfect No. 1 Duke 81, No. 9 TCU 58 — 127 perfect No. 2 Houston 88, No. 10 Texas A&M 57 — 120 perfect No. 11 Texas 74, No. 3 Gonzaga 68 — 27 perfect No. 3 Illinois 76, No. 11 VCU 55 — 26 perfect No. 4 Nebraska 74, No. 5 Vanderbilt 72 — 4 perfect No. 4 Arkansas 94, No. 12 High Point 88 — 4 perfect 3:42 am, March 22, 2026 Arkansas is back in the Sweet 16. No. 4 Arkansas knocked off No. 12 High Point, 94-88. It was a back-and-forth affair that was tied with three minutes to go, but the Panthers didn’t quite have enough to upset the Razorbacks. High Point chucked up 38 3-pointers, only converting on 10 of them. But, seemingly every time High Point needed a bucket, its seniors delivered to keep them in the game. Rob Martin had a 30-point, five assist performance while Cam’Ron Fletcher added 25 points and eight rebounds. But Arkansas proved to be too much. The Razorbacks had four double-digit scorers, led by All-American freshman Darius Acuff Jr., who scored 36 points, shooting 50 percent to go along with six assists, to go along with double-doubles from senior Malique Ewin (14 points, 12 rebounds) and sophomore Billy Richmond III (15 points, 10 rebounds). Arkansas advances to play the winner of No. 1 Arizona and No. 9 Utah State in the Sweet 16. Perfect bracket tracker: None of the four remaining perfect brackets had High Point advancing. The remaining four perfect brackets will move onto day four of the men’s basketball tournament. 3:03 am, March 22, 2026 The dream run continues for Nebraska. No. 4 Nebraska took down No. 5 Vanderbilt, 74-72, in an absolute thriller. Nebraska freshman Braden Frager gave the Cornhuskers the go-ahead shot with 2.2 seconds left before sophomore Commodore Tyler Tanner took a half court shot that just narrowly rattled out, ending Vanderbilt's season. Those two were clutch for their respective teams down the stretch. Tanner led Vanderbilt with 27 points to go along with four assists and four steals, including the near game-winner that would've gone down in history. Frager came off the bench, scoring 15 points on a 6 of 11 shooting night, including the go-ahead bucket. Nebraska advances to play the winner of No. 1 Florida and No. 9 Iowa in the program's first-ever Sweet 16 appearance. Perfect Bracket Tracker: And then there were four. All but four of the remaining perfect brackets across major online games had Vanderbilt moving on. Of the remaining sites, two perfect brackets remain in the Men's Bracket Challenge Game and two remain on ESPN.
